utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, can you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Case Number IT-97-25/1-PT, the Prosecutor versus Mitar Rasevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. For the Prosecution, Mr. Bill Smith, and my name is Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: Appearances for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Branko Lukic for Mitar Rasevic, today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: Hello to you both. Mr. Rasevic, can you hear the proceeding in a language you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. We will proceed with further appearance of the accused Mitar Rasevic, pursuant to Rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. And we start directly with the pleading. Mr. Rasevic, during your initial appearance on 18 August this year, you stated that you received the indictment in a language you understand, that you read it, and that you understand its content. And you also explicitly waived your right to have the indictment read in its entirety. Do you stand by this statement even today, or shall we read the indictment to you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I stand by my previous statement. I fully understood the indictment, and there's no need for the indictment to be read back to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: Thank you for that. And so are you now ready to plead, Mr. Rasevic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, when I first appeared before this Tribunal on the 18th of August, I intended to enter a plea. However, the counsel that I had required to represent me before this Court could not be present there. Even a month later, the counsel that I had in mind for representing me here could not be brought here. And until such request is met in a satisfactory way, and I have given my terms, I will not be ready to enter any kind of plea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. You can sit down. So we will proceed under the Rule 62, count 4, which states that "a Judge shall, if the accused fails to enter a plea at the initial or any further appearance, enter a plea of not guilty on the accused's behalf." So pursuant to Rule 62 IV, I hereby enter a plea of not guilty for all counts on the behalf of Mitar Rasevic. And I will go through the indictment now and read the counts and a plea of not guilty applies to all the counts. So the first count against you is a charge of persecution on political, racial, and religious grounds, being a crime against humanity. Accused pleads not guilty. The second count is a charge of torture as a crime against humanity. Again, not guilty. The third count is a charge of torture as a grave breach of the Geneva Convention of 1949. Not guilty. The fourth count is a charge of torture as a violation of the laws or customs of war. Not guilty. The fifth count is a charge of inhumane acts as a crime against humanity. Not guilty. The sixth count is a charge of willfully causing serious injury to body or health, being a grave breach of Geneva Convention. Not guilty. The seventh count is a charge of cruel treatment as a violation of the laws or customs of war. Not guilty. The eighth count is a charge of murder as a crime against humanity. Not guilty. The ninth count is a charge of willful killing as a grave breach of Geneva Convention. Not guilty. The tenth count is a charge of murder as a violation of the laws or customs of war. Not guilty. The eleventh count is a charge of imprisonment as a crime against humanity. Not guilty. The 12th count is a charge of unlawful confinement of civilian as a grave breach of the Geneva Convention. Not guilty. The 13th count is a charge of inhumane acts as a crime against humanity. Not guilty. The 14th count is a charge of willful causing of grave suffering Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. as a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions. Not guilty. The 15th count is a charge of cruel treatment as a violation of the laws or customs of war. Not guilty. The 16th count is a charge of enslavement as a crime against humanity. Not guilty. The 17th count is a charge of inhumane treatment as a grave breach of Geneva Conventions. Not guilty. The 18th and last count is a charge of slavery as a violation of the laws or customs of war. Not guilty. I would like, Madam Registrar, to note, I would like you to note that a plea of not guilty was entered on behalf of Mr. Mitar Rasevic to all the counts of the indictment. And also, Mr. Rasevic, I would like to inform you that pursuant to Rule 62 bis, you may change this plea of not guilty to guilty in any relation to some or all counts at any later stage of the proceeding. And now, I would turn to Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic, I think we should discuss a little bit the -- I would like to know -- I would like to see where we are standing in relation of appointment of permanent Defence counsel, if you can advise me on this subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like, Your Honour, to be able to advise you on that matter, but I'm afraid that it would be -- that that question should be put to the Registrar because right now, I am talking with Mr. Rasevic. We have contact, but he prepared his defence with another Defence attorney who was a mediator in between the Tribunal and Mr. Rasevic in connection with his voluntary surrender. And that's why Mr. Rasevic is a bit surprised why his counsel is not allowed to defend him during these proceedings. So we all hope that that matter would be solved soon and that Mr. Rasevic would have appointed lawyer by his choice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, please, can you give me the name of this lawyer who is cooperating with the accused?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I know that the first lawyer who brought -- who came here with Mr. Rasevic was Mr. Slavisa Prodanovic. And as I learned from the Registrar, there is some kind of investigation against Mr. Prodanovic, but the second choice of Mr. Rasevic is my colleague from Belgrade, Mr. Kolesar. So I don't know what the Registrar decided regarding this lawyer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: I was informed by the registry that pursuant to the directive on assignment of Defence counsel, both those counsels you named and which were requested by the accused are not eligible for appointment. So because you are the counsel, present counsel, of Mr. Rasevic, I would be very happy if you could advise him on the decision which was -- decision of the President. I don't know if you are aware of this. It's a decision of the President on assignment of Defence counsel. It's in -- it's from 20th of August. And it indicates the Prosecutor versus Vaselin Sljivancanin. So would you be so kind to use this decision and explain the situation to Mr. Rasevic. Maybe in the light of this decision, he will choose any other counsel from the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will do my best. And I think that Mr. Rasevic has been misinformed regarding this decision because he heard in the Detention Unit that Mr. Sljivancanin was approved, those counsel were approved to defend Mr. Sljivancanin. So obviously he is not informed correctly. I can explain him the decision because I read the decision and I know the substance of the decision. I will assist the Registrar as long as it's necessary, and I really hope that the permanent counsel will be appointed to Mr. Rasevic as soon as possible because as we know, as of today, his deadlines for objections to the indictment would start. So in the next 30 days, he should have somebody who would be able to object if there is anything to be objected regarding this indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you fully. So thank you for this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: So other issues I would like to deal with is to instruct the Registrar to fix a day for a trial when appropriate, taking into consideration, Madam Registrar, what was said here by Mr. Lukic concerning the problems with the counsel. And I will schedule this Status Conference pursuant to Rule 65 bis(A) to be heard within 120 days in order to facilitate the preparation of the trial. You will, both parties, be informed of the exact day in due course. In the meantime, the accused will remain in custody, but may file an application for provisional release pursuant to Rule 65. Concerning OTP, I would like to know, I was informed by my legal staff that the supporting material has been served directly upon the accused. Is that correct, Madam?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there any matter that the Prosecution wishes to raise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: The same question for the Defence, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: So I think we have dealt with all the points. So thank you for attending. And I will adjourn the proceeding.
